title: Website Design in Sterling, Illinois: A Whiteside County Guide

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a fictional manufacturing capability sheet, quote form, and precision metal part; not a photograph of a Sterling factory.

figures.title: Build the site around a procurement inquiry
figures.summary: The manufacturing section describes a different information path from a walk-in business.

items.label: Discover capabilities
items.detail: Explain the manufacturing processes and work the company can take on.

items.label: Review specifications
items.detail: Make relevant technical sheets easy to find.

items.label: Evaluate the fit
items.detail: Use clear capability content to help a buyer decide whether to ask for a quote.

items.label: Request a quote
items.detail: Provide an RFQ path suited to the information the business needs.

figures.caption: A conceptual B2B customer path from the article, not a claim about any specific Sterling manufacturer.

figures.title: Check the industrial content before selecting a template
figures.summary: A manufacturing site should support the buyer's task, not copy a restaurant's structure.

items.label: Capability pages
items.detail: Give each important capability enough space to be understood.

items.label: Specification access
items.detail: Organize the documents a prospective buyer needs.

items.label: RFQ form
items.detail: Make the request route clear and appropriate for technical inquiries.

items.label: Local business details
items.detail: Keep location, service area, and public contact information consistent.
